issues.detail: The Greek 'ουτως' (outōs) means 'thus' or 'in this way,' which is missing in the Vietnamese translation. Furthermore, the Vietnamese 'những kẻ' (those who/people who) adds a plural noun that is not present in the Greek; the Greek 'συ κρατουντας' refers to 'you holding' (singular/plural person), but the Vietnamese phrasing shifts the focus to a group of people as an object rather than the action of the subject.
